new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has no record and no existing statements for Reshe; this is the first opened source that says anything prosodic: lexical tone is present and (partly) transcribed; no stress statement. Compatible with Harris 1946 (already held by the project, silent on stress and tone). download route: rogerblench.info direct still serves an sgcaptcha meta-refresh (HTTP 202); obtained archived copy (Internet Archive, 28 May 2025) via --connect-to 207.241.237.2.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Reshe is treated as a tone language: the sound-system sketch has consonant and vowel charts plus a 'Tones' paragraph, about 360 headwords carry acute/grave tone marks (e.g. á-bákèndó 'animal', àmá 'throw', á-pínə́ 'buttocks') and two entries are annotated 'no tones' (i.e. tone not recorded). Nothing anywhere in the document about stress, accent or prominence (a full-text search for stress/accent: stress/accent/pitch/prominence/syllable = 0 hits).
new_statements.identity_note: Dettweiler & Dettweiler's own data are from Pisabu ('central' Reshe, near Yelwa/Yauri, Kebbi State), compared with a Shabanda ('northern') list; a speaker reports Shabanda speech as slower with different intonation. Blench's dictionary pools Harris 1939/1946, BCCW (Shabanda), his 1989 fieldnotes, the Dettweiler Pisabu list and Agamalafiya 2004, tone-checked with Rev. Appollos Agamalafiya at Bin Yauri (2008).
